sequence_description: Brokered OIDC SSO connector: mint a custom JWT id_token-like artifact signed by an attacker key (or with mismatched iss) and attempt to use it for login via the OIDC SSO connector path. Include a control password login to validate baseline.
description: [LLM-Judge] The sequence intended to validate rejection of an attacker-signed/mismatched-issuer OIDC id_token, but the observed successful login was via SAML and provides no evidence the forged OIDC token was accepted.

evidence.llm_judge_description: The sequence intended to validate rejection of an attacker-signed/mismatched-issuer OIDC id_token, but the observed successful login was via SAML and provides no evidence the forged OIDC token was accepted.

sequence_description: SAML OneTimeUse replay: perform a SAML login with OneTimeUse and a fixed Assertion/@ID, then replay the exact same assertion ID again; SP must reject the second use.
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML replay attempt failed due to an invalid/missing SAML connector (session.invalid_connector_id) rather than an explicit OneTimeUse/assertion replay rejection, so the test did not actually validate replay protection.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML replay attempt failed due to an invalid/missing SAML connector (session.invalid_connector_id) rather than an explicit OneTimeUse/assertion replay rejection, so the test did not actually validate replay protection.

sequence_description: I2 revocation freshness: revoke an access token then verify it is no longer active via introspection; include a second identity control token to ensure introspection works.
description: [LLM-Judge] Revocation attempt failed with invalid_client, so the token was never revoked; post-revoke introspection remaining active indicates revocation endpoint/client-auth misconfiguration rather than confirmed token-revocation bypass.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Revocation attempt failed with invalid_client, so the token was never revoked; post-revoke introspection remaining active indicates revocation endpoint/client-auth misconfiguration rather than confirmed token-revocation bypass.

sequence_description: I2 OIDC SSO callback replay defense: attempt brokered OIDC SSO login where IdP omits nonce (mock behavior) and ensure RP rejects; include a second identity password login as control.
description: [LLM-Judge] OIDC SSO login succeeded even though the IdP omitted the nonce, indicating missing/ineffective nonce validation and potential callback replay/login CSRF risk.

evidence.llm_judge_description: OIDC SSO login succeeded even though the IdP omitted the nonce, indicating missing/ineffective nonce validation and potential callback replay/login CSRF risk.

sequence_description: I2 anti-replay across grants: obtain a subject access token, revoke it, then attempt RFC8693 token exchange using the revoked subject_token; include a second identity control exchange using a non-revoked token.
description: [LLM-Judge] Revocation step failed with invalid_client (401), so the test did not actually revoke the subject token; anti-replay-after-revocation behavior cannot be validated and may indicate a misconfigured/unauthenticated revocation endpoint.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Revocation step failed with invalid_client (401), so the test did not actually revoke the subject token; anti-replay-after-revocation behavior cannot be validated and may indicate a misconfigured/unauthenticated revocation endpoint.

sequence_description: Refresh-token replay after revocation: obtain a refresh_token, revoke it, then attempt to use the same refresh_token again to mint a new access token.
description: [LLM-Judge] Revocation step failed with invalid_client (401), so refresh-token revocation was not performed and the replay-after-revocation security property was not actually tested.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Revocation step failed with invalid_client (401), so refresh-token revocation was not performed and the replay-after-revocation security property was not actually tested.

sequence_description: Attempt to replay the same OIDC authorization code twice at /oidc/token (auth code must be one-time). Includes a second identity password-login control to ensure the environment is functional.
description: [LLM-Judge] Authorization code exchange failed (invalid_grant) and yet the captured identity for the failed exchange is Bob’s identity, suggesting possible identity mix-up/leakage in error-path handling or test harness attribution.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Authorization code exchange failed (invalid_grant) and yet the captured identity for the failed exchange is Bob’s identity, suggesting possible identity mix-up/leakage in error-path handling or test harness attribution.

sequence_description: Obtain a subject access token under the test app context, then attempt RFC8693 token exchange using a different client context (M2M client credentials). Verify the exchange is rejected or remains properly bound (no cross-client splicing). Includes introspection of the subject token as control evidence.
description: [LLM-Judge] M2M access token appears to be accepted for token issuance (HTTP 200) but then rejected as invalid on subsequent identity verification (HTTP 401), suggesting inconsistent token validation/audience handling.

evidence.llm_judge_description: M2M access token appears to be accepted for token issuance (HTTP 200) but then rejected as invalid on subsequent identity verification (HTTP 401), suggesting inconsistent token validation/audience handling.

sequence_description: RFC8693 token exchange coherence: obtain a subject token for API resource A, then attempt to exchange it for a token targeting a different audience/resource B (should be rejected or remain properly bound). Includes introspection evidence and a second identity control.
description: [LLM-Judge] Introspection reports the freshly obtained subject session token as inactive (active=false) despite successful login, suggesting broken introspection, wrong token type, or token binding/issuance inconsistency.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Introspection reports the freshly obtained subject session token as inactive (active=false) despite successful login, suggesting broken introspection, wrong token type, or token binding/issuance inconsistency.

sequence_description: I3 state-swap / session-splice attempt: start two parallel OIDC auth requests with different state values, then attempt to exchange the auth code from session A while presenting state from session B (should be rejected). Includes a password-login control to ensure environment is functional.
description: [LLM-Judge] Token exchange correctly failed (invalid_grant), but the failed exchange response/runtime capture appears to leak or mis-associate an identity (Bob) to Alice’s token exchange attempt.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Token exchange correctly failed (invalid_grant), but the failed exchange response/runtime capture appears to leak or mis-associate an identity (Bob) to Alice’s token exchange attempt.

sequence_description: I4 attack: attempt account takeover by logging in via OIDC SSO with email_verified=false but email matching an existing local user; platform must not collapse attacker principal into victim subject.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SSO login produced a new subject but reused an existing local user's email/display_name, which is suspicious and could indicate unsafe attribute-based profile merging/linking behavior.

sequence_description: Cross-connector collision: create a second OIDC SSO connector and attempt to authenticate the same email with different upstream sub across connectors; verify identities do not collapse unexpectedly due to connector target confusion.
description: [LLM-Judge] Cross-connector account collision: two different SSO connector logins resolved to the same internal identity/entity_id, indicating identities can collapse across connectors (likely keyed only by email or mis-scoped subject).

sequence_description: Cross-protocol principal collision attempt: create a local password user (victim). Then SSO-login as an attacker principal using the same email but first with email_verified=false (should NOT map to victim), then flip to email_verified=true and re-login (should still not collapse into victim if principal binding is strict).
description: [LLM-Judge] SSO principal with the victim’s email (initially email_verified=false, later flipped to true) remained a separate identity and did not collapse into the existing local-password victim account; this is safe if the platform binds by IdP subject/connector, but it is suspicious because the SSO identity is allowed to assert an email already owned by another account without any visible conflict/verification step.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SSO principal with the victim’s email (initially email_verified=false, later flipped to true) remained a separate identity and did not collapse into the existing local-password victim account; this is safe if the platform binds by IdP subject/connector, but it is suspicious because the SSO identity is allowed to assert an email already owned by another account without any visible conflict/verification step.
